record.paper_title: Open problems in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
record.original_question: For edge colorings of line segments in Euclidean space, call a finite line-segment configuration E edge-Ramsey if, for every number of colors r, every sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space has the property that any r-coloring of its line segments contains a monochromatic copy of E. Is the edge set of a regular hexagon not edge-Ramsey?

evidence.quote: we will say that E is edge-Ramsey
Conjecture 8 The edge set of a regular hexagon is not edge-Ramsey.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in Euclidean spaces $\mathbb{R}^n$, and regard a line segment as an unordered pair $\{x,y\}$ of distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^n$. A finite configuration of line segments is a finite set $E$ of such segments (considered up to Euclidean congruence). Given a positive integer $r$, an $r$-coloring of the line segments in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is an assignment of one of $r$ colors to every line segment in $\mathbb{R}^n$. A monochromatic copy of $E$ in such a coloring is an image of $E$ under a Euclidean isometry of $\mathbb{R}^n$ all of whose segments receive the same color.

Call a finite line-segment configuration $E$ edge-Ramsey if for every positive integer $r$ there exists $N=N(E,r)$ such that for every $n\ge N$ and every $r$-coloring of the line segments of $\mathbb{R}^n$, there is a monochromatic copy of $E$.

Let $H$ be the set of six edges of a regular hexagon in the plane (each edge regarded as a line segment between two adjacent vertices).

Prove or disprove: $H$ is not edge-Ramsey.
artifact.status_search_result: Surveys on Euclidean Ramsey theory list the question of whether the edge set of a regular hexagon is edge-Ramsey as an open conjecture. Regular n-gons are known to be edge-Ramsey for n=2,3,4, but the hexagon case remains unresolved, and no general characterization of edge-Ramsey configurations is known.

status_evidence.title: 11 Euclidean Ramsey Theory (Handbook chapter)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses edge-Ramsey configurations and lists open problems including the status of regular polygons.
status_evidence.claim: The edge-Ramsey status of the regular hexagon is treated as an open conjecture in the standard survey.

status_evidence.title: Old and new Euclidean Ramsey theorems
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces edge-Ramsey notion and discusses which polygon edge sets are known to be edge-Ramsey.
status_evidence.claim: Edge-Ramsey is established for small regular polygons but the hexagon case is not resolved.
